previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of chronic pancreatitis, type 2 diabetes, hypertension, bipolar disorder, PTSD, and alcohol abuse in remission was admitted for severe abdominal pain worsening over ten days, associated with nausea, vomiting, and one episode of hematemesis. He developed a pruritic rash after fentanyl administration and had a brief episode of eye fluttering without loss of consciousness. Imaging revealed two large pancreatic duct stones causing obstruction and progressive dilation of the pancreatic duct to 10 mm. His pain was managed with IV and then oral hydromorphone, and he advanced to a regular diet. The ERCP team was consulted and will schedule an outpatient stone extraction. He was discharged home with medication refills and instructions to follow up with his primary care provider and gastroenterology team.
